correctness.rationale: For every 0≤a<1 the exact covariance is (1+a²)I/4, giving K(x,y)=1+4x·y/(1+a²). On the outer boundary the squared radius is uniform in [A_t,B_t]; integration of angular h yields the exact divided-difference formula. Strict convex chord inequality gives (3−t)L(t)<(1−t)g(A_t)+2g(B_t), hence L′(t)<0. Kernel-sign maximizers and positivity indicators yield sharp attainment. Endpoint expansions follow from differentiation and the shrinking-interval midpoint. Algebra and ten numerical quadrature cases were checked from the embedded code; these finite checks do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: Removing a concentric hole changes the sampling distribution in a canonical least-squares problem. The theorem establishes a strict stability improvement for all hole radii rather than only computing isolated constants: it gives the exact continuum profile, all norming evaluation locations, positivity defect, a quadratic small-hole law and a linear thin-ring approach. The nontrivial monotonicity requires a sharp radial convexity/chord comparison and helps distinguish area loss from boundary-only sampling.
